overview: Enprise Group is a small-cap NZX-listed technology holding company built around Kilimanjaro Consulting, the largest MYOB Acumatica and MYOB Exo implementation and support partner in Australia and New Zealand, alongside a majority stake in HubSpot-focused digital agency Recipe Marketing, a controlling stake in cloud quoting SaaS business iSell (ITQuoter), and minority stakes in Datagate Innovation (32.35%, billing/reporting SaaS for telecom/utility resellers) and Vadacom Holdings (6.4%, cloud VoIP). The Group's strategy is to act as an investment vehicle that acquires and grows complementary trans-Tasman tech businesses, but it remains overwhelmingly dependent on Kilimanjaro's MYOB consulting revenue, which is transitioning from legacy on-premise Exo software (now being wound down by MYOB) to the cloud-based Acumatica ERP platform.

business_model.summary: Enprise earns most of its revenue from professional services and software resale/support margins tied to implementing and supporting third-party MYOB ERP software (Acumatica and the legacy Exo product) for mid-market businesses in NZ and Australia, supplemented by recurring SaaS subscription revenue from its own iSell (ITQuoter) quoting product and Recipe Marketing's HubSpot-based digital marketing/consulting services. Revenue is a mix of project-based implementation/consulting fees (largest, lower-margin, cyclical with client IT capex), recurring software licence and hosting/support fees (higher margin, stickier), and Recipe Marketing's marketing services fees. FY2026 revenue of $26.3m grew 6% but was accompanied by a net loss of $2.2m (vs a $0.1m loss in FY2025), driven by employee cost growth (+14% to $21.3m) outpacing revenue and a $1.08m intangible impairment. Group operating margins have been negative or near breakeven every year since FY2018, reflecting thin-margin consulting economics and repeated impairments/write-offs.

revenue_streams.name: Services and support (Kilimanjaro consulting/implementation)
revenue_streams.notes: FY26: $15.53m (+6.5% YoY). Largest and most labour-intensive stream; project-based implementation and ongoing support for Acumatica/Exo clients.

revenue_streams.name: Enterprise software licences
revenue_streams.notes: FY26: $7.34m (+11.5% YoY), including recurring Acumatica subscription licences. Management highlights this as the higher-quality, more recurring component.

revenue_streams.name: Hosting services
revenue_streams.notes: FY26: $1.69m (down from $1.97m), reflecting legacy Exo-hosted clients migrating off or churning as MYOB winds down Exo.

revenue_streams.name: iSell (ITQuoter SaaS)
revenue_streams.notes: FY26: $1.73m. Cloud quoting software for Managed Service Providers, sold in AU, UK/Europe, NZ, South Africa and North America; 72.5%-owned subsidiary.

business_model.customer_type: B2B — mid-market businesses (Kilimanjaro's Acumatica/Exo client base spans ~350 Acumatica clients and ~800 legacy Exo clients) and Managed Service Providers (iSell's MSP customer base). No single large enterprise or government customer concentration disclosed, but the business is dependent on MYOB as its software supplier/platform partner.
business_model.geographic_mix: FY26: Australia $18.7m (71%), New Zealand $7.3m (28%), EMEA/North America together <1%. Australia has grown to be the dominant market and continues to grow faster than NZ.

main_competitors: Other MYOB Acumatica/Exo implementation partners in Australia and NZ (e.g. Ndevr, Momentum Software Solutions, Auboros, Stratus Group) competing for the Exo-to-Acumatica migration wave

Acumatica implementation partners more broadly, and rival mid-market ERP ecosystems (NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, SAP Business One, Xero + add-ons) competing for the same mid-market ERP replacement spend
Larger, better-capitalised IT consulting/systems-integration firms that can bundle ERP implementation with broader digital transformation services
HubSpot competitors and other digital marketing agencies for Recipe Marketing
Alternative SaaS billing/quoting vendors competing with iSell and Datagate in their respective niches
competitive_position.market_position: Kilimanjaro is described (by the company and third parties) as MYOB's largest/number one Acumatica and Exo implementation partner in Australia and New Zealand, with an installed base of roughly 350 Acumatica and 800 legacy Exo clients — a genuine leadership position in a narrow niche. However, Enprise itself is a micro-cap (market capitalisation roughly NZ$11-12m as of September 2026) with limited balance-sheet capacity, thin margins, and a going-concern qualification noted by the NZ Shareholders' Association following FY2025 accounts.

moat_factors.description: ~800 legacy Exo clients and ~350 Acumatica clients represent embedded relationships with high switching costs once an ERP system is implemented and staff are trained. This installed base generates recurring support/hosting revenue and a pipeline of migration projects as Exo is sunset.

moat_factors.factor: Scale within a narrow niche ('best partner standing')
moat_factors.description: Management explicitly frames its strategy as being the leading Acumatica/Exo partner in the region, leveraging deep product expertise built over ~20 years since Kilimanjaro's founding. This specialisation is difficult for generalist IT consultancies to replicate quickly, but it is also a narrow moat confined to one vendor's ecosystem.

Enprise's fortunes are tied to MYOB's product roadmap and partner economics. MYOB, not Enprise, controls software IP, pricing, and platform direction — Enprise captures implementation/services margin but has limited pricing power over the core product.

Stakes in Recipe Marketing (52%), iSell (72.5%), Datagate (32.35%) and Vadacom (6.4%) provide some diversification beyond MYOB consulting, and management points to 'synergies' across the portfolio, but none of these businesses are large enough yet to offset Kilimanjaro's dominance of group results.

weaknesses: Extremely small scale (market cap ~NZ$11-12m, revenue ~NZ$26m) limits capital-raising options, negotiating leverage with MYOB, and ability to absorb shocks

History of thin or negative operating margins and repeated goodwill/intangible impairments (FY2023: $7.7m impairment on a $10.6m loss; FY2026: $1.08m impairment) points to weak underlying earnings power and past overpayment for acquisitions
Revenue and profitability heavily concentrated in Kilimanjaro/MYOB ecosystem — a single-vendor dependency risk with no disclosed hedge if MYOB's strategy shifts adversely

Deteriorating liquidity: NZSA flagged a current ratio of 0.66 (current liabilities exceed current assets) and debt-to-equity of 3.80 alongside a formal going-concern qualification in FY2025 audited accounts
Governance gaps flagged by NZSA: lack of CEO KPI transparency, no published skills matrix, no disclosed whistleblowing policy, and a share buyback pursued despite the going-concern warning

growth_drivers: MYOB Exo end-of-life migration wave: MYOB Exo Payroll license renewals ended November 2025 and compliance updates cease October 2026, forcing ~800 legacy Exo clients in Enprise's installed base to migrate to Acumatica or an alternative platform over the next 1-2 years — a substantial, largely captive project pipeline if Kilimanjaro can retain and convert these clients ('best partner standing' strategy).

Acumatica recurring licence growth: recurring revenue from enterprise software licences grew ~12% in FY26 and continues to be highlighted by management as the highest-quality, most scalable revenue stream, with further AI-related feature investment by Acumatica (and HubSpot, via Recipe Marketing) seen as a demand driver for implementation and consulting services.

Recipe Marketing / HubSpot cross-sell: Recipe Marketing achieved HubSpot Diamond Partner status and ranks in the top 10 HubSpot partners in the JPAC region; management cites 'exceptional growth' and synergies with Kilimanjaro's client base as a cross-sell opportunity.

Australian market expansion: Australia is already ~71% of group revenue and has grown faster than New Zealand; continued mid-market technology investment in Australia, plus an improving business-confidence backdrop cited by management, could support further growth.

iSell/ITQuoter international expansion: iSell sells into Australia, UK/Europe, New Zealand, South Africa and North America, giving a small but genuinely global SaaS distribution footprint that could scale with more investment.

Portfolio monetisation optionality: the Datagate Innovation stake (32.35%) has been the subject of an investor update on 'valuation and exit considerations' (July 2026), raising the possibility of a value-crystallising sale or listing that could improve Enprise's balance sheet.

business.description: The great majority of group revenue flows through Kilimanjaro's relationship with MYOB's Acumatica and Exo products. Any adverse change in MYOB's partner economics, product strategy, or competitive positioning versus NetSuite/Dynamics/Xero would directly impair Enprise's core earnings engine.

FY2026 letter from the board explicitly cites 'ongoing margin pressure in consulting services' amid competitive market conditions in NZ and Australia; employee costs grew faster (14%) than revenue (6%) in FY2026, compressing already-thin margins into a net loss.

While the Exo sunset creates a migration opportunity, it also creates churn risk — clients could choose a competing Acumatica partner, a rival ERP platform entirely, or delay/cancel migration, eroding the existing hosting/support revenue base before new Acumatica revenue fully replaces it.

Impairments of intangibles/goodwill in multiple recent years (FY2023 $7.7m; FY2026 $1.08m) suggest a pattern of acquisitions or capitalised assets not delivering expected returns, raising the risk of further write-downs on Recipe Marketing, iSell or Datagate carrying values.

financial.risk: Going concern qualification and weak liquidity
financial.description: FY2025 audited accounts carried a material uncertainty regarding going concern per NZSA's review; current ratio of 0.66 (current liabilities exceed current assets by roughly $3.2m) and debt-to-equity of 3.80 leave very little balance sheet buffer. FY2026 net assets fell further to $1.56m (from $3.06m in FY2025) on the year's net loss.

Net tangible assets per share were negative at FY2026 year-end (-$0.10/share, from -$0.06/share in FY2025). Total liabilities of $13.3m against total assets of $14.8m leave minimal equity cushion; a further loss-making year could push the Group toward negative shareholders' equity.

financial.risk: Reliance on rights issues to fund operations
financial.description: The Group has repeatedly raised small amounts of capital via rights issues (2023: ~$1.32m of a $1.74m target; December 2025/January 2026: ~$1.0m total including shortfall shares), diluting existing shareholders and signalling recurring cash needs rather than organic self-funding.

BNZ's $1.0m overdraft facility and a $221k commercial loan (maturing 24 April 2026, secured over substantially all Group assets) represent near-term refinancing/covenant risk for a company already flagged for going-concern uncertainty.

regulatory.risk: NZX continuous disclosure and governance compliance
regulatory.description: As a smaller NZX-listed issuer with governance gaps already flagged by NZSA (CEO incentive disclosure, skills matrix, whistleblowing policy), Enprise faces reputational and compliance risk if disclosure standards are not lifted, though no specific regulatory action has been reported.

With ~71% of revenue now generated in Australia through an NZ-domiciled parent, cross-border tax structuring and transfer pricing between NZ and Australian subsidiaries is an ongoing but manageable compliance consideration typical of trans-Tasman groups.

macro.description: Kilimanjaro's consulting revenue depends on mid-market businesses committing to ERP implementation projects — discretionary capital and change-management spending that slows in weaker economic conditions. Management noted 'economic headwinds' and 'subdued market conditions in NZ and Australia' through FY2026.

Group carries floating-rate bank overdraft (9.26% at Dec-2025) and commercial loan (6.93%) facilities; while absolute debt is small, high effective interest rates on a company already loss-making add to cash burn.
With Australia now ~71% of revenue, AUD/NZD movements affect translated group results, though the Group has historically shown only modest foreign currency translation reserve movements.

execution.description: Managing Director and CEO Ronnie Baskind — who founded Kilimanjaro Consulting and had led the Group for roughly 20 years, credited by the Board as instrumental to its success — departed effective 4 September 2026, shortly after the Board itself called FY2026 results 'unacceptable.' Grant Harwood was appointed interim CEO while a permanent search proceeds, overseen by a board Transition Committee. Leadership change immediately following a poor result and amid a formal 'strategic reset' materially raises execution risk at a critical juncture.

Independent director Aaron Ridgway resigned effective 30 April 2026; new directors Susan Stone (May 2025) and Gina Tuzcet (January 2026) recently joined. Elevated board turnover concurrent with the CEO transition adds to institutional-knowledge and continuity risk during the strategic review.

Following the FY2026 loss, the Board has undertaken 'a comprehensive review of strategic priorities, financial position and operating model.' The scope, cost, and outcome of this review (which could include further impairments, divestitures such as the flagged Datagate exit consideration, headcount reductions, or a further capital raise) are not yet known and represent a significant near-term catalyst/risk in either direction.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Mid-market ERP/cloud accounting software implementation remains a structurally growing niche as SMEs continue migrating from legacy on-premise systems to cloud platforms, reinforced in Enprise's specific case by MYOB's decision to sunset the legacy Exo product (license renewals ended November 2025, compliance support ends October 2026) and concentrate investment in cloud-native Acumatica. This creates a finite, multi-year forced-migration tailwind for MYOB's implementation partner ecosystem, of which Kilimanjaro is a leading player, but it is a narrow (single-vendor) rather than broad industry tailwind.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — consulting/implementation revenue is discretionary IT capex that softens in weaker economic conditions (management explicitly cited subdued NZ/Australia market conditions through FY2026), while recurring software licence, hosting and SaaS revenue (iSell, Recipe Marketing subscriptions) provide a partial, non-cyclical offset.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct sensitivity given a small absolute debt/overdraft balance, but elevated for a company already loss-making and cash-constrained — every basis point of financing cost matters more when net assets and liquidity buffers are thin.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Moderate and growing — Australia is now ~71% of Group revenue (up from historically lower levels), so AUD/NZD movements increasingly influence translated results, though historically this has been immaterial to reported earnings.
key_input_costs: Skilled ERP/software consulting labour (Australia and NZ) — employee expense is the dominant cost line (~81% of revenue in FY2026) and grew faster than revenue, the single biggest driver of the FY2026 loss
MYOB software licensing/partner economics — Enprise's margin on software revenue is set in large part by its commercial terms with MYOB as platform vendor
Office/technology overheads and cloud hosting costs supporting the Exo-hosted client base

recent_developments.event: Ronnie Baskind's employment as Managing Director and CEO ended 4 September 2026; he transitioned to a Non-Executive Director role. Baskind founded Kilimanjaro Consulting and led the Group for roughly 20 years. Grant Harwood appointed Interim CEO with immediate effect; a Transition Committee (chaired by director Susie Stone, with Gina Tuzcet and Nick Paul) established to oversee the handover while a permanent CEO search proceeds.

FY2026 full-year results (year ended 30 June 2026) released 31 August 2026: revenue grew 6% to $26.3m, but the Group posted a net loss of $2.2m (vs a $0.1m loss in FY2025), including a $1.08m intangible asset impairment (largely attributed to Kilimanjaro). Employee costs rose 14% to $21.3m, outpacing revenue growth. Basic/diluted loss per share was (9.67) cents. The Chairman called the result 'unacceptable' and announced a comprehensive review of strategic priorities, financial position and operating model to reset the business for sustainable profitability. Net assets fell to $1.56m (from $3.06m); net tangible assets per share turned more negative at -$0.10/share.

Ronnie Baskind's departure as Managing Director/CEO first announced 30 July 2026 (employment end date 4 September 2026). Separately, a Datagate Innovation Q1 2026 investor update addressed valuation and 'exit considerations' for Enprise's 32.35% stake, raising the possibility of a future sale or monetisation event.
Independent Non-Executive Director Aaron Ridgway resigned effective 30 April 2026, contributing to elevated board turnover during the year.

H1 FY2026 results (six months to 31 December 2025) released: revenue of $12.95m (+3.5% YoY), an operating loss of $0.62m (vs a $0.12m operating profit in 1H FY25), and a net loss attributable to shareholders of $0.54m (vs a $0.15m profit in 1H FY25). Basic/diluted EPS was (2.71) cents. Kilimanjaro's segment recorded an operating loss of $0.38m on higher employment costs and lower utilisation; iSell remained profitable ($0.06m); Recipe Marketing described as showing 'exceptional growth' and strong HubSpot/Kilimanjaro synergies. Employee costs rose to $10.37m (1H FY25: $9.16m).

2025 Annual Shareholders' Meeting held 3 December 2025. NZ Shareholders' Association review (based on FY2025 audited accounts) flagged: a going-concern material uncertainty from the auditor, current ratio of 0.66, debt-to-equity of 3.80, and multiple governance disclosure gaps (CEO incentive KPI transparency, no skills matrix, no disclosed whistleblowing policy). NZSA specifically questioned a proposed share buyback given the going-concern warning and weak liquidity.

Rights issue completed: on 31 December 2025 the Group issued 1,729,277 shares at $0.45/share (~$0.76m raised); a further 275,228 shortfall shares were allotted 14 January 2026 at the same price (~$0.12m), taking total capital raised to roughly $1.0m across the two tranches. Total shares on issue increased from ~20.06m to ~22.06m.
Gina Tuzcet appointed to the Board as a Non-Executive Director effective 2 January 2026 (status formally clarified 3 February 2026).

H1 FY2025 (to 31 Dec 2024) had shown net profit of $0.15m and operating profit of $0.12m — the comparative base against which FY2026's deterioration into losses is most visible, underscoring that FY2026's margin compression is a genuine year-on-year decline rather than a one-off.

guidance.as_of: FY2026 results announcement (31 August 2026) and H1 FY2026 report (27 February 2026)

items.notes: Enprise does not issue formal quantitative revenue or earnings guidance in its results announcements or interim reports. The FY2026 results announcement instead commits to a 'comprehensive review of strategic priorities, financial position and operating model' with the stated goal of 'a return to sustainable profitability,' but no specific targets, timeline, or numeric range have been disclosed as of the FY2026 announcement.

items.target: Qualitative commitment to return to sustainable profitability
items.notes: Announced alongside FY2026 results; outcome (cost reduction, portfolio changes, capital structure actions) not yet detailed. New permanent CEO appointment (search ongoing under interim CEO Grant Harwood) likely to shape or restate strategy once concluded.
Management repeatedly emphasises growing recurring software licence revenue (+12% in FY26) and the Exo-to-Acumatica migration opportunity as the core growth narrative, but without numeric targets.

guidance.management_commentary: H1 FY2026 letter from the Board (27 February 2026): 'Market conditions remain competitive across New Zealand and Australia, with ongoing margin pressure in consulting services. The Group continues to focus on improving utilisation, maintaining cost discipline, and growing recurring revenue streams across its software platforms. The Board remains committed to strengthening operating performance and maintaining balance sheet stability.' FY2026 results commentary (31 August 2026): Board regards the result as 'unacceptable' and has taken 'decisive action to reset the business for a return to sustainable profitability' following 'subdued market conditions in NZ and Australia.'

bull_case: Kilimanjaro holds a genuine leadership position as MYOB's largest Acumatica/Exo implementation partner in Australia/NZ, with ~800 legacy Exo clients facing a forced migration deadline (Exo compliance support ends October 2026) — a substantial, semi-captive project pipeline if Kilimanjaro executes the conversion well.

Recurring, higher-margin revenue (Acumatica software licences, hosting/support, iSell and Recipe Marketing SaaS subscriptions) is growing faster than the lower-margin consulting base, and Recipe Marketing's HubSpot Diamond Partner status/top-10 JPAC ranking suggests a genuinely successful adjacent growth bet.

The FY2026 'unacceptable result' and CEO/board reset could be the catalyst for a genuine operational turnaround: a new interim/permanent CEO, an explicit strategic review, and potential monetisation of the Datagate stake all create optionality for meaningful value creation from a very low starting market capitalisation (~NZ$11-12m).

Extremely small size and depressed valuation (stock down ~44% over the past year per market data) mean even a modest return to sustained profitability or a successful Datagate exit could be disproportionately positive for the share price relative to its current base.
Trans-Tasman diversification (Australia now ~71% of revenue) reduces single-country concentration risk and taps a larger addressable mid-market ERP opportunity than NZ alone.
bear_case: Going-concern uncertainty flagged by the auditor on FY2025 accounts, a current ratio of 0.66, debt-to-equity of 3.80, and further deterioration in FY2026 (net assets down from $3.06m to $1.56m, negative net tangible assets per share) point to a fragile balance sheet with very limited room for further setbacks.

Leadership instability at the worst possible time: the CEO who built the company over ~20 years departed within weeks of the Board itself calling results 'unacceptable,' alongside a resigning independent director and a board still absorbing two other very recent appointments — high execution risk exactly when a turnaround needs stability.

Structural dependency on a single third-party software vendor (MYOB) for the great majority of earnings leaves Enprise with limited pricing power and full exposure to MYOB's own strategic decisions (which have already forced a costly and uncertain Exo-to-Acumatica client migration).

A history of recurring intangible/goodwill impairments (FY2023: $7.7m; FY2026: $1.08m) and repeated small dilutive rights issues (2023, and again Dec-2025/Jan-2026) suggests a pattern of value destruction and a business that has not demonstrated it can self-fund growth.

Governance red flags identified by the NZ Shareholders' Association (opaque CEO incentive structure, no skills matrix, no disclosed whistleblowing policy, a share buyback pursued despite a going-concern warning) raise questions about board oversight quality precisely when rigorous oversight is most needed.
